topic: Using std::fill and std::fill_n for Assigning Values to Ranges
explanation: In modern C++, std::fill and std::fill_n are algorithms used to assign a specific value to a range of elements within a container or sequence. They are essential for efficiently initializing or resetting elements in containers such as vectors, arrays, or other iterators. These functions promote clear, concise, and expressive code by abstracting manual loops, and they are part of the Standard Template Library (STL), leveraging iterator concepts for flexibility and generic programming.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of std::fill to assign the value 5 to all elements in the vector, effectively initializing or resetting the container. Then, std::fill_n assigns the value 10 to the first three elements of the vector. The code showcases how these algorithms simplify bulk value assignment over ranges, leveraging iterators for flexibility and adhering to modern C++ best practices.
